Original review:
They refused to see me because I was one minute late for check in and they had no regard for the fact im wheelchair bound, im suffering from cancer and its incredibly difficult for me to get to and through the health centre. I’m also autistic and get time blindness which means under the 2010 equality act this practice should be making reasonable adjustments such as moving the appointment a few minutes later, not making me feel even worse when my mental health is already through the floor and I contemplate cancelling my life on a daily basis. They said all they could do is arrange a telephone call weeks later, I’ll probably be dead by then. I literally said as I left “see you later if im still alive” because I genuinely hope I never have to see them again as no other business makes me feel so useless and disregarded. I cannot continue to live in this state of health but I am on my own with no support so getting to appointments is incredibly difficult for me. Every other company I’ve dealt with are more than happy to make reasonable adjustments for disabled customers, I don’t know why it’s so hard for these people. The GPs themselves are actually quite nice, on the rare occasions I’m able to see them. Most of the time I’m stopped by bureaucracy like the time flicking over to 1451 when apparently check in closed at 1450 so that’s it they just send you home.
